overlapping_phenotypes: ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm, tall stature, pectus excavatum/carinatum, scoliosis, arachnodactyly
discriminating_logic: Presence of ectopia lentis is cardinal hallmark of Marfan syndrome and canonically absent in LDS6; arterial tortuosity strongly favors LDS spectrum.

overlapping_phenotypes: progressive thoracic aortic aneurysm, diffuse peripheral arterial aneurysms, arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism
discriminating_logic: Bifid uvula and craniosynostosis are frequent in LDS1/2 (55-62% of carriers) but absent (0%) or exceptionally rare in SMAD2 carriers.

overlapping_phenotypes: marfanoid habitus, thoracic aortic aneurysm, aortic root dilation, hypertelorism, camptodactyly
discriminating_logic: Significant intellectual disability and craniosynostosis are cardinal diagnostic criteria for Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome but absent in typical adult-onset familial LDS6.

overlapping_phenotypes: early spontaneous arterial dissection, rupture of hollow viscera, easy bruising, translucent skin
discriminating_logic: Aortic root aneurysm is characteristic of SMAD2 (present in 66.7%), whereas COL3A1 vasculopathy typically causes dissections of medium-sized muscular arteries without antecedent root aneurysm dilation.
